text:
<!--
  THE AGENT'S JOB DESCRIPTION — editable capability text, same as prompt.md.

  Everything below is sent to the agent as its first user message, so it is part of the
  skill you are optimizing: reword it, restructure it, add or remove guidance, change the
  interaction contract. This comment block is STRIPPED before the agent sees it.

  LOAD-BEARING PLACEHOLDERS — these are filled in per task and must SURVIVE any edit:
    {instruction} {spreadsheet_path} {spreadsheet_content} {instruction_type}
    {answer_position} {output_path}
  Optional: {max_turns}. No other {braces} are allowed.

  If a required placeholder goes missing, or an unknown one appears, the candidate is
  REJECTED before any task runs — the agent would otherwise be told to write its answer to
  a path it was never given. A literal brace must be doubled: {{ or }}.
-->
You need to solve the following spreadsheet manipulation question. It contains six pieces of information:
- instruction: the question about spreadsheet manipulation.
- spreadsheet_path: the path of the spreadsheet file you need to manipulate.
- spreadsheet_content: the target range's total size, the location of the other graded copies
  of this workbook, each sheet's real data extent, and the first few rows of the content.
- instruction_type: Cell-Level Manipulation (answer_position is exact cell(s)) or Sheet-Level Manipulation (answer_position is the maximum range you may modify).
- answer_position: the cell(s)/range you must modify or fill in.
- output_path: write the modified spreadsheet file to this exact path.

### instruction
{instruction}

### spreadsheet_path
{spreadsheet_path}

### spreadsheet_content
{spreadsheet_content}

### instruction_type
{instruction_type}

### answer_position
{answer_position}

### output_path
{output_path}

You have up to {max_turns} rounds. Each round, reply with EXACTLY ONE ```python fenced code
block and nothing outside it (a reply with no code block runs nothing and wastes the round;
keep reasoning to short `#` comments inside the block). Follow these turns in order:

TURN 1 — INSPECT ONLY (print; do NOT save). Your FIRST code block must only load the workbook
and PRINT what is really there — it must NOT compute the answer, write cells, or save an output
file yet. Print, by coordinate:
   - the sheet names;
   - the full header row(s) of every sheet you will read from or write to;
   - the column LETTER that holds each field the instruction names — confirm each one, do not
     trust the preview's labels. Two columns can share a word, and the key you filter or look up
     on is frequently in a DIFFERENT column from the raw-data column with the same header.
   - the row where real data STARTS and the row where it ENDS;
   - the current contents of answer_position and the cells directly to its left and above it.
Never guess a column or row from the preview: it may relabel headers (`Unnamed: N`), merge two
headers onto one line, hide that the first row(s) are a header, or show only the first rows.

TURN 2+ — SOLVE AND VERIFY IN ONE SELF-CONTAINED BLOCK. Using the coordinates you just
confirmed, write ONE block that does all of the following, in order:
   (a) load spreadsheet_path fresh;
   (b) COMPUTE each answer cell from the data it just read (never hardcode a value from the
       preview — this exact block is re-run on other copies whose data differs);
   (c) write ONLY the target cell(s) with openpyxl and save to output_path (create missing
       parent directories first);
   (d) re-open output_path and PRINT every cell in answer_position to check your work.
This block must STAND ALONE — load input → save output → read back — because it, unchanged, is
what grades you, and on the other copies only their own input file exists. NEVER put the
read-back (step d) in a separate later reply that just opens output_path without first doing
(a)–(c): on the other copies that output file does not exist yet, so such a block writes nothing
and scores 0. Your final code block is always the complete self-contained solve+read-back block.

Confirm from the printed read-back that ALL of these hold before you finish:
   - every target cell holds the intended value;
   - the type is right (number stored as a number, float where the result is fractional, text
     left as text — not converted to a date/number);
   - no cell OUTSIDE answer_position changed, and every other sheet is still present.
If any check fails, fix the block and re-run the WHOLE self-contained block. Reply WITHOUT a
code block only after a self-contained solve+read-back block has printed the target cells and
all three checks hold.
If your code raises an error, the traceback is returned to you; read it and fix the code — do
not resend the same code unchanged.
